channel.title: Hlido — AI agent reviews
channel.description: Independent C2PA-verified reviews of AI agents. Every claim tested, scored on the Laddoo scale, signed with cryptographic provenance.

item.title: Parrot — Laddoo 81/100
item.description: A privacy-first, open-source meeting assistant for Mac that helps during the call, not just after — and backs its local-first promise with specifics rather than slogans.

item.title: Craft Agents — Laddoo 79/100
item.description: An open-source desktop agent interface built to connect to anything — MCP, APIs, local files, and a built-in Chromium browser — with bring-your-own-model breadth that is genuinely broad.

item.title: Lancetta — Laddoo 78/100
item.description: A free, native menu-bar app that reads your Codex and Claude Code quota and tells you when to push, slow down or switch — and shows its working under every suggestion.

item.title: Praex — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: An open-source, multi-surface coding copartner — terminal, phone and web on one session — that runs on the maker's own models or your keys, and is free to start. The models themselves are the unproven part.

item.title: Navige — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: An in-path cost-governance layer that sits between your AI agents and the models they pay for, acting before a run rather than reporting after it — thoughtfully built and strikingly honest, but with no traction or pricing yet on show.

item.title: Pentest-AI — Laddoo 81/100
item.description: An open-source pentest agent whose whole design point is refusing to report a finding it cannot reproduce three times.

item.title: Jacquard (formerly Phrasee) — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: An established enterprise marketing-language vendor, now rebranded to Jacquard and repositioned as an agentic layer - credible product, zero public price, and headline statistics we cannot check.

item.title: WiseVision ROS2 MCP — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: An MPL-2.0 MCP server that puts a ROS 2 robot fleet behind a tool interface an agent can read and - deliberately optionally - drive.

item.title: Graphicle (KarLex AI) — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A local, Apache-2.0 code-graph and memory layer that returns cited excerpts to coding agents - genuinely useful, genuinely version 0.1.1.

item.title: Superset — Laddoo 69/100
item.description: A polished multi-agent coding workspace that you cannot currently use - the primary call to action is a waitlist, and the product is mid-rename.

item.title: Tofu — Laddoo 79/100
item.description: Turns an app your coding agent just built into something other people can actually open - one paste, a real URL, and a published price.

item.title: Offrun — Laddoo 78/100
item.description: A free Mac workspace for running several coding agents side by side, whose best feature is the unglamorous one: it shows you exactly how much quota each account has left.

item.title: Agent 37 — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: A cloud sandbox for agents that publishes its unit rates, shows its own cost comparison with sources, and offers to refund the difference - the price transparency is the product.

item.title: Traceforce — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: On-device security and control for AI agents - the right architecture for where AI actually runs, sold with trust claims that name no customer and no price.

item.title: Viberia — Laddoo 62/100
item.description: A game-styled desktop console for running many coding agents at once - an appealing idea shipped on a page that was still rendering placeholder text when we captured it.

item.title: Arena42 (Agent Arena) — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: An active, legible competition arena where AI agents play games and earn credits — a genuinely agent-native product whose surface is clear but whose headline stats and earnings model stay unverified.

item.title: Clawezy — Laddoo 67/100
item.description: A managed one-click deployment of an OpenClaw chat-agent to your own server, with refreshingly transparent pricing — thin on security specifics and leaning on generic social proof.

item.title: Broxi AI — Laddoo 63/100
item.description: A well-presented done-for-you agent deployment service — strong on articulating a process, weak on anything a buyer can verify before a sales call.

item.title: OpenChatCut — Laddoo 77/100
item.description: An open-source, AI-assisted video editor that keeps the human on a real timeline — credible OSS traction, MCP-connectable, with a clear open-vs-Pro split.

item.title: Docker Agent — Laddoo 83/100
item.description: Agents defined in YAML and run like containers — a clean, developer-honest tool from Docker with first-class CLI, HTTP API, MCP and A2A, let down only by what a docs read cannot verify.

item.title: Agor (by Preset) — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: A 'multiplayer AI' workspace that puts team and agents on one shared board — strong operate/governance thinking and a real agent surface, with the usual unknowns of an unexercised product.

item.title: agent.reviews — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: A novel review platform where coding agents — not humans — write the reviews of developer tools, with detailed, specific entries as evidence the mechanism works, and the obvious open question of how far to trust them.

item.title: pocketty — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A tightly-built iPhone/iPad SSH companion for answering blocked coding agents from your pocket — serious about end-to-end security and upfront about a one-time price, but bound to the 'herdr' orchestrator.

item.title: Iris — Laddoo 62/100
item.description: A coherent enterprise pitch for custom 'operations' agents that run across your existing tools — but the entire product sits behind a 'book a demo' wall, so almost none of it is checkable from the outside.

item.title: Recurse — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: Hosting-for-agent-apps that treats MCP as the output format — build an agent app, deploy it with one CLI command, publish it as an MCP any client can call. Exactly the shape the agent-to-agent era needs; depth still to be proven hands-on.

item.title: Sparrow — Laddoo 68/100
item.description: Open-source, self-hostable 'message rooms' for humans and their agents — a trust-friendly take on the agent inbox problem, but an early one with a thin public surface.

item.title: OpenAPPA — Laddoo 64/100
item.description: A deterministic, policy-as-code guardrail for agents with real technical ambition (paper, benchmarks, OPA/Cedar comparisons) — undercut by a '100% resistant to data exfiltration' absolute that no security product should make.

item.title: RxFilmStudio — Laddoo 60/100
item.description: A native macOS 'film studio in one window' — score, narrate, caption and render with an agent in the director's chair. Polished pitch for creators, but it's a downloadable desktop app Hlido could not run, so the verdict is about the surface only.

item.title: Raven (EverMind) — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A multi-agent orchestration layer that sits above the coding agents you already run (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Qwen and more) — real GitHub traction and broad interop, wrapped in heavy 'self-evolving / RSI' language that the surface can't back up.

item.title: DevMate.AI — Laddoo 40/100
item.description: An AI-coding landing page with enterprise-grade claims and toy-grade evidence — big compliance promises, nothing on the public surface to back them.

item.title: ENZO — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: A self-hosted, bring-your-own-keys AI command center with a genuinely strong key-custody story — let down on the surface by rough edges and a pricing table that says nothing.

item.title: Foremerge — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: A deterministic, MCP-first coordination protocol for multi-agent coding — unusually honest about its own limits, and exactly the plumbing a fleet-of-agents future needs.

item.title: OtoDock — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: A self-hosted 'agentic company OS' on your own Claude/Codex subscription, with an unusually specific security model — ambitious in breadth, still asking to be taken on trust on most of it.

item.title: Radix — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A genuinely agent-native idea — a persistent visual workspace where a coding agent builds artifacts wired to your repo — behind a deliberately minimal, key-gated landing that gives Hlido almost nothing to verify.

item.title: rustunnel — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: An open-source, Rust-fast tunnel with a first-class MCP server — genuinely agent-drivable, priced to punish idle time, but the managed edge and reliability claims are asserted, not yet independently run.

item.title: Hello Aria — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: A chat-native personal productivity assistant that reaches you where you already are — WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, web and iOS — with real Google and Microsoft integrations, held back by marketing hype and thin trust transparency.

item.title: Driven — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A coherent, transparently-priced AI investment agent with broad market coverage — but its autonomous-execution headline is still aspirational and its trust claims lean on unverifiable social proof.

item.title: trace-mcp — Laddoo 77/100
item.description: A genuinely agent-native code-intelligence MCP server — open-source, local-first, broadly integrated — whose headline token-savings claims are asserted without a published, reproducible benchmark.

item.title: GoSQLX — Laddoo 75/100
item.description: A fast, well-presented multi-dialect SQL parsing SDK for Go with a genuinely agent-first MCP surface — but its headline performance and traction numbers are vendor-asserted and, in one case, don't reconcile.

item.title: kestra-io/mcp-server-python — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A credible, well-documented MCP server that exposes Kestra's workflow orchestration to agent clients like Claude, Cursor and VS Code — genuinely agent-first, though Hlido's capture landed on the parent blog rather than the repo, leaving repo-health signals unverified.

item.title: AceDataCloud MCP Nano Banana — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: A genuinely MCP-native image-generation server — four clean tools over Google's Nano Banana via AceDataCloud — but a thin, MIT-licensed wrapper whose reliability, traction, and image provenance all rest on an unverified third-party gateway.

item.title: Winx — Laddoo 78/100
item.description: A Rust MCP server that gives a coding agent a real PTY-backed shell with unusually careful safety engineering — impressively thorough for a project only days old.

item.title: medical-mcp — Laddoo 68/100
item.description: A broad, key-free MCP server over FDA, WHO, PubMed and RxNorm that installs in one click — but its privacy promise and its Google Scholar leg do not sit comfortably together.

item.title: Marzban — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: Marzban — open-source (AGPL-3.0) proxy-management panel: web UI, REST API, Telegram bot, multi-admin, multi-server scaling. Mature community project, docs navigated cleanly by our engine; capabilities self-described, nothing deployed. Infrastructure, not an AI agent. Tier-2 review; medium confidence.

item.title: Harden — Laddoo 85/100
item.description: Harden — local pre-execution monitor that checks coding-agent tool calls before they run (blocked/allowed/made-safe, on-device logs). Evidence-forward surface with live demo and baselined benchmarks; all figures self-reported. Tier-2 public-surface review; medium confidence.

item.title: Loqua — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: Loqua — AI voice dictation for Mac/Windows: global shortcut into any app, real-time cleanup, screenshot answers. Clear promise and accessible trial; headline numbers unverified and little exercisable public surface. Tier-2 review; medium confidence.

item.title: Concord AI — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A coordination layer for multi-agent coding — genuinely agent-native and unusually honest about its own evidence, but still waitlist-stage with the Cloud tier unshipped.

item.title: Mode — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: An AI design canvas that edits your real codebase — a sharp answer to throwaway-mockup drift, with transparent pricing but a login-gated product we couldn't run.

item.title: Naseem — Laddoo 79/100
item.description: A Mac-native coding agent with an unusually rigorous 'prove, don't assert' philosophy and transparent BYO-key pricing — genuinely differentiated, though young and untested by us behind the download.

item.title: Ouroboros — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: An open-source (MIT) spec-and-verify harness that sits around your coding agent — a strong idea with broad host support, still early and unverified by us at runtime.
